title: kv-cache attention kernel seqlen edgecase notes
content:
Purpose / context:
- quick personal breadcrumbs for the weird perf/regression we keep hitting when seq_len crosses ~2048 boundary (seen on gpt-like models, test with gpt-j-6b and llama-7b).
- Symptoms: sudden latency spike + occasional OOM-like allocation failure during long context generation; sometimes cache sanity-checks show missing prefixes.

Observed on:
- infra: dedicated dev node (p4d.24xlarge-ish), cuda 12.1, cudnn 8.3, pytorch 2.2 build with custom kernels
- runtime: serving-runtime v0.27.1 (local branch with KV cache refactor)
- models: gpt-j-6b (fp16), llama-7b (int8/ptq), toy reproducer small_gpt for unit tests

Quick repro steps (local):
1) start server: 
   ATTENTION_KERNEL_AUTO=1 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python -m redwood.runtime.server --port 8080 --config tests/local_kv_seqlen_config.yaml &
2) run generator with long prompt: 
   python tools/infer.py --host localhost:8080 --model gpt-j-6b --batch-size 1 --max-tokens 2048 --prompt-file tests/seqlen_boundary_prompt.txt
3) incrementally bump prompt by 256 tokens until 2304/2560 and watch logs.

Commands tried (notes inline):
- forced kernel hint: RI_KERNEL_HINT=flash_attn_v2 -> avoids spike in many cases (but not all).
- forced kernel hint: RI_KERNEL_HINT=cutlass_gemm -> stable but slower overall; no OOM observed.
- disable kv-cache: --kv-cache-enabled=false -> no regression, but throughput drops (expected).
- tried smaller batch-size (1->.5 not possible) -> issue persists, suggests per-request seq_len dimension matters more than batch.

Key log snippets (trimmed):
- [2025-11-05 14:22:11] INFO select_kernel: seq_len=2048, heads=32, head_dim=128, selected=flash_attn_v2
- [2025-11-05 14:22:12] WARN kv_cache: eviction_count=0, expected_entries=2048, actual_entries=2039
- [2025-11-05 14:22:12] ERROR allocator: failed to allocate pinned buffer size=201326592 -> fallback to pageable (higher latency)
- [2025-11-05 14:22:12] INFO select_kernel: seq_len=2049, heads=32, head_dim=128, selected=cutlass_gemm
- [2025-11-05 14:22:12] ERROR generation: prefix_lookup_mismatch idx=2038 expected_offset=... got=... (off-by-one?)

Hypotheses (ordered by priority):
1) kernel-selection threshold off-by-one around 2048 -> triggers a different code path that assumes contiguous kv cache layout; the other kernel expects different layout/packing and we fail to translate offsets correctly.
2) KV cache indexing arithmetic uses int32 vs int64 and overflows/rounding near boundary (not full overflow but sign/clip behavior causing missing entries).
3) pinned-memory allocator heuristics fail when allocation rounding crosses 192 MB boundary -> runtime falls back to pageable memory and latency spikes; the fallback code path does a sync-copy that invalidates assumptions in the cache metadata.
4) quantization/layout differences (int8 kernels use different qkv packing) — when runtime switches kernel it fails to reformat cached KV blobs.
5) concurrent garbage-collection/eviction races: when seq_len increases rapidly we evict while other thread reading causing index mismatches.

What we've ruled out:
- Not purely model-specific: seen on both gpt-j and llama family.
- Not purely hardware: reproduced on local dev and in Dedicated staging (different GPU vendors).
- Not caused by batch_size = 0 issue (we run batch=1 in reproducer).

Small reproducer unit test (pseudo):
- make tests/kv_seqlen_boundary_test.py with a deterministic pseudo-model (tiny) that uses same kv cache layout and toggles selection logic. Steps: fill cache with seq_len N, then append single token with seq_len N+1 and assert offsets consistent.
- current quick script: tests/repro_kv_seqlen_boundary.sh -> runs python small_server + client that appends tokens; see attached repro in linked_artifacts (PR 892 contains test harness).

Notes on kernel selection code (where to look):
- serving-runtime/kernel_selector.cpp: line ~420 threshold = heuristic(heads, head_dim, seq_len, sm) -> returns enum
- runtime/kv/cache_manager.py: serialize/deserialize methods for kv blocks; check pack/unpack for alignments (16/32 byte)
- allocator/pinned_pool.cc: fallback path logs and sync-copy logic

Immediate experiments to run (next 48h):
- add assert checks in cache_manager when deserializing: check base pointers and expected sizes, fail early with diagnostics to see index math.
- instrument kernel_selector to log full heuristic input (sm, free_mem, warps_per_sm) to see why it flips at 2049.
- force ATTENTION_KERNEL_AUTO=0 and set RI_KERNEL_HINT=cutlass_gemm to see if that universally avoids failure (works as workaround).
- run repro under cuda-memcheck/asan to detect illegal accesses (may be slow).
- add unit test that simulates switching kernel while cache holds packed int8 vs fp16 blobs; ensure we convert properly.

Short-term mitigation for staging:
- set default kernel hint for large sequences to cutlass_gemm until we confirm fix.
- add metrics: kernel_switch_count, kv_cache_mismatch_count, pinned_fallback_count to monitor frequency (console + Prom).

Open questions / unknowns:
- Are there model-specific packing differences we missed? e.g., gpt-j qkv layout consistent with llama?
- Is the allocator fallback happening before or after the cache write? logs ambiguous.
- Could small rounding in heuristic cause flip for some GPUs only? need to capture sm/capability in logs.

Notes to self (messy):
- saw one trace where selected kernel flipped twice in same request (2048 -> cutlass -> flash_attn) which seems wrong unless we re-evaluate mid-request. Need to dump kernel selection timestamps.
- maybe we only re-evaluate on token boundaries when seq_len % 256 == 1 (something in policy). search for re-eval triggers in runtime/router.cpp

TODO (priority):
- [ ] add extra diagnostics in cache_manager deserialize (Samira)
- [ ] add verbose kernel_selector logging (Liam)
- [ ] reproduce under cuda-memcheck on smaller model (Priya)
- [ ] temp config: default large-seq kernel=cutlass_gemm in staging config (ops)
- [ ] write unit test for kernel-switch + kv cache consistency (blocking PR)

If you pick this up: start with logs for 2025-11-05 14:22:11..14:22:14 in staging node a-3 (id in ops slack), grep for select_kernel, kv_cache, allocator. Add to PR description any failing asserts.

Random scratch bits:
- quick math used for heuristic: cost_est = seq_len * head_dim * heads * 2 (approx) -> maybe overflow?
- alignment pads: pack_size = ((seq_len * head_dim + 31) / 32) * 32 -> check integer divisions.

End of notes.
